1. A refused phone command can expose its secret 🐞 Bug ⛨ Security
>
>Description >
> >
>_decide passes the typed job id through match_job_id and then publishes and logs its error
>verbatim when the final token authenticates the command. If someone enters the command secret as
>both the job id and the final token, the resulting no such job reason contains that secret in the
>notification and daemon log.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[src/hands/phone.py[R426-427]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/pull/4/files#diff-6d175ae5f33f6b544ecf5e01493181c805135928b88647bc51a3ff9971544b75R426-R427) > >```diff >+ if job_id is None: >+ return await self._refuse(verb, missing) >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>match_job_id includes the caller's typed value in its missing-job error. The new
>authenticated-refusal path forwards that error to _refuse, which both logs it and passes it to
>Notifier.answer for publication.
>
> > [src/hands/api.py\[184-201\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/d50af2a99203bf98a3b4a628daf4227b1466e8c4/src/hands/api.py/#L184-L201) > [src/hands/phone.py\[416-444\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/d50af2a99203bf98a3b4a628daf4227b1466e8c4/src/hands/phone.py/#L416-L444) > [src/hands/notify.py\[337-347\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/d50af2a99203bf98a3b4a628daf4227b1466e8c4/src/hands/notify.py/#L337-L347) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >An authenticated phone decision can echo a mistyped job id containing the command secret into a notification and log. >## Fix Focus Areas >- src/hands/phone.py[416-444] >- src/hands/api.py[174-201] >## Recommended Fix >Keep untrusted typed ids out of published and logged refusal reasons, including ambiguous-id errors. Add a test that supplies the secret as both job id and final token and checks notifications and logs. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

2. Discotrade reviews stop after restarts 🔗 Cross-repo conflict ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>Adding aux.orphaned to the events that hands routes makes a restarted review reach the playbook,
>but discotrade's PLAYBOOK.toml has no rule for that event. When a discotrade review is orphaned,
>hands stops its pipeline instead of resending the review prompt.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[src/hands/playbook.py[153]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/pull/4/files#diff-d4c45908377a317f0fbbccad6f8af7a74c4af564c4272d3cecc7126bf1be9204R153-R153) > >```diff >+ "aux.orphaned", # §39 (H-057): a review the daemon's stop (or a crash) killed >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The PR admits the orphan event into routing. Discotrade routes completed reviews to the architect
>but defines no aux-orphan rule; hands stops when a routed event has no candidate rule.
>
> > [hands -> discotrade](https://app.qodo.ai/management/relationships?repoId=77e6b9e3-9009-4fbe-bd8c-e1c4bd92a98f&relatedRepoId=f8bc154f-fef0-4515-a253-775ba818fa12&view=table) > [src/hands/playbook.py\[150-154\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/d50af2a99203bf98a3b4a628daf4227b1466e8c4/src/hands/playbook.py/#L150-L154) > [src/hands/playbook.py\[1774-1790\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/d50af2a99203bf98a3b4a628daf4227b1466e8c4/src/hands/playbook.py/#L1774-L1790) > [External repo: SigorMatt/discotrade, PLAYBOOK.toml \[76-115\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/discotrade/blob/4549e57788ceda8f5c3799a53d827ca5ebda9150/PLAYBOOK.toml/#L76-L115) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >The new `aux.orphaned` event reaches discotrade's playbook, which has no matching rule, so a restarted review stops the pipeline. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- /cross_repos/discotrade/PLAYBOOK.toml[108-117] >- src/hands/playbook.py[150-154] > >## Recommended Fix >Coordinate a discotrade playbook update adding `aux.orphaned → resume`, and deploy that playbook alongside the new hands behavior. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

3. The review command alters the repository 📘 Rule violation ⛨ Security
>
>Description >
> >
>archive creates directories and writes hosted comments and JSON files directly under the
>repository. Running hands hosted-review therefore performs filesystem writes and invokes gh api,
>rather than remaining limited to hands commands and read-only repository inspection.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[src/hands/hosted.py[R156-161]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/pull/4/files#diff-12a5dbbc969c160015a0fe085926cb598038c83131b13d5d84d1da86343eed7eR156-R161) > >```diff >+def archive(base: Path, k: int, comments: list[tuple[str, dict[str, Any]]]) -> Path: >+ target = base / str(k) >+ target.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False) >+ for kind, obj in comments: >+ name = f"{kind}-{obj['id']}" >+ (target / f"{name}.md").write_bytes(_body(obj).encode("utf-8")) >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The command implementation added in this PR invokes gh api and creates repository directories and
>files with mkdir, write_bytes, and write_text, which directly conflicts with the checklist's
>read-only driver requirements.
>
> > Rule 3255328: [Restrict driver to read-only operations within CLONE directory](https://app.qodo.ai/rules/3255328?state=active) > [src/hands/hosted.py\[91-108\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/d50af2a99203bf98a3b4a628daf4227b1466e8c4/src/hands/hosted.py/#L91-L108) > [src/hands/hosted.py\[156-164\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/d50af2a99203bf98a3b4a628daf4227b1466e8c4/src/hands/hosted.py/#L156-L164) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >The hosted review command writes archived review data into the repository and invokes an external `gh` command, conflicting with the read-only driver restriction. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- src/hands/hosted.py[91-108] >- src/hands/hosted.py[156-165] > >## Recommended Fix >Keep the driver-side review operation read-only and route archival through an explicitly authorized non-driver component, or revise the command boundary so repository writes cannot occur in the driver implementation. Preserve explicit failure handling for the external API call and ensure any archival destination is separately authorized. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

>Description >

>meta/FINAL-REPORT-23.md records short commit identifiers and prose summaries of test runs without
>full SHAs or verbatim tool output. When readers rely on the report to verify the claimed units and
>checks, they cannot reproduce the exact commits, counts, messages, or line references from the
>report itself.
>
>
>

> >[meta/FINAL-REPORT-23.md[R18-20]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/pull/4/files#diff-ec307b17764eaea292c820a1f8767eb101d2c72a2676bff1b962445255d27fd5R18-R20) > >```diff >+- U0 b7b5c10 (`plan:`): meta/plan.md, meta/CHECKPOINT.md, meta/journal.md, >+ meta/findings/FINDINGS.md (H-055..H-060 filed; H-051..H-054 set to >+ "decided (DESIGN §39, mission 23 U)"). Green 3/3, 4387 passed. >``` >

>Evidence >

>The final report lists abbreviated SHAs such as b7b5c10 and narrative claims such as `Green 3/3,
>4387 passed`, while its test section describes outputs without reproducing the raw command output

Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >The final report uses abbreviated commit identifiers and summarizes test results without including exact integer metrics and raw command output. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- meta/FINAL-REPORT-23.md[16-20] >- meta/FINAL-REPORT-23.md[128-134] > >## Recommended Fix >Replace each abbreviated commit reference with the full commit SHA, add explicit test and failure counts for every reported check, and include clearly marked verbatim raw output sections for the test, lint, and other external tool invocations discussed in the report. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

5. Hosted reviews hide the verdict 📘 Rule violation ✧ Quality
>
>Description >
> >
>run prints the pull-request summary and archive location before it emits the eventual verdict:
>line, and the verdict is lower-case rather than a leading VERDICT: line. Every human-visible
>hosted review therefore begins with counts and archive metadata instead of the required verdict
>prefix.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[src/hands/hosted.py[R333-335]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/pull/4/files#diff-12a5dbbc969c160015a0fe085926cb598038c83131b13d5d84d1da86343eed7eR333-R335) > >```diff >+ counts = {kind: sum(1 for k_, _ in comments if k_ == kind) for _, kind in SOURCES} >+ print(f"PR #{pr}, {bot}: " + ", ".join(f"{kind}s {n}" for kind, n in counts.items()), >+ file=out) >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The new renderer prints PR #... and archive/count information before reaching the verdict
>branches, while those branches emit verdict: rather than a first-line VERDICT: prefix.
>
> > Rule 3255377: [Prefix human-visible reports with a `VERDICT:` line](https://app.qodo.ai/rules/3255377?state=active) > [src/hands/hosted.py\[333-335\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/d50af2a99203bf98a3b4a628daf4227b1466e8c4/src/hands/hosted.py/#L333-L335) > [src/hands/hosted.py\[376-388\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/d50af2a99203bf98a3b4a628daf4227b1466e8c4/src/hands/hosted.py/#L376-L388) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >The hosted review renderer emits summary and archive lines before its verdict and formats the verdict with a lower-case prefix. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- src/hands/hosted.py[333-335] >- src/hands/hosted.py[376-388] > >## Recommended Fix >Determine the Code Review verdict before rendering the report, print a first line beginning exactly with `VERDICT:`, and then emit counts, archive metadata, findings, and details on subsequent lines. Use the active verdict vocabulary and preserve the no-review state as an explicit non-clean verdict. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

6. A failed archive leaves a false review fetch 🐞 Bug ☼ Reliability
>
>Description >
> >
>archive creates the numbered directory before writing its comment files, while run returns an
>error without removing files already written. If a later write fails, the next invocation counts
>that incomplete directory as a previous fetch and diffs against it.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[src/hands/hosted.py[R158-161]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/pull/4/files#diff-12a5dbbc969c160015a0fe085926cb598038c83131b13d5d84d1da86343eed7eR158-R161) > >```diff >+ target.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False) >+ for kind, obj in comments: >+ name = f"{kind}-{obj['id']}" >+ (target / f"{name}.md").write_bytes(_body(obj).encode("utf-8")) >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>Writes happen sequentially after directory creation, the error handler performs no cleanup, and
>_numbered accepts any numeric directory as an earlier fetch.
>
> > [src/hands/hosted.py\[146-165\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/d50af2a99203bf98a3b4a628daf4227b1466e8c4/src/hands/hosted.py/#L146-L165) > [src/hands/hosted.py\[315-331\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/d50af2a99203bf98a3b4a628daf4227b1466e8c4/src/hands/hosted.py/#L315-L331) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >A write failure can leave an incomplete numbered hosted-review archive that a later run treats as a completed fetch. >## Fix Focus Areas >- src/hands/hosted.py[146-165] >- src/hands/hosted.py[315-331] >## Recommended Fix >Write the complete fetch into a temporary directory, remove it on failure, and move it to the numbered archive path only after every write succeeds. Test a failure after one comment has been written. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

>
>
>Code >
> >[driver/hooks/bash_guard.py[R653-654]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/pull/4/files#diff-19f2ab92dd12e6110ca94a59853d99703e4636cababa636d2003000b7b53a974R653-R654) > >```diff >+ self.docs = docs >+ roots = [clone, spool] + ([kits, docs] if role == ARCHITECT_ROLE else []) >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The guard accepts every path beneath each read root, and the configured source-tree fallback for
>HANDS_DOCS is the repository root.

8. A misparsed Code Review reads as a clean review 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>run takes findings(body) as the whole truth: when _FINDING matches no `<summary>N.
>…</summary> block, it prints verdict: no finding open in the Code Review comment (it numbers
>none) and exits 0, even if the header counts it just parsed with categories()` say there are
>findings. A small change in the bot's markup (a <b> around the number, a different list tag, say)
>would turn a review with open findings into a pass, and both the builder's last unit and the
>reviewer's sub-agent rely on this verdict.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[src/hands/hosted.py[R386-389]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/pull/4/files#diff-12a5dbbc969c160015a0fe085926cb598038c83131b13d5d84d1da86343eed7eR386-R389) > >```diff >+ else: >+ note = f"{len(current)} resolved" if current else "it numbers none" >+ print(f"verdict: no finding open in the Code Review comment ({note})", file=out) >+ return 0 >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>categories() (lines 196-199) pulls counts such as Bugs (3) from the header, but nothing compares
>them with len(current). With zero parsed findings the else branch reports "no finding open" and
>returns 0. docs/QODO-EXTRACTION.md line 31 makes this comment the only source of the verdict, so a
>parse that finds nothing silently becomes a clean review.
>
> > [src/hands/hosted.py\[196-220\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/d50af2a99203bf98a3b4a628daf4227b1466e8c4/src/hands/hosted.py/#L196-L220) > [src/hands/hosted.py\[376-389\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/d50af2a99203bf98a3b4a628daf4227b1466e8c4/src/hands/hosted.py/#L376-L389) > [docs/QODO-EXTRACTION.md\[12-31\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/d50af2a99203bf98a3b4a628daf4227b1466e8c4/docs/QODO-EXTRACTION.md/#L12-L31) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >`hands hosted-review` exits 0 with "no finding open" whenever the findings regex matches nothing, even when the header counts say findings exist. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- src/hands/hosted.py[196-220] >- src/hands/hosted.py[376-389] > >## Recommended Fix >Parse the number in each header category label (`(\d+)`) and add them up. If the total is above zero and `findings(body)` returns fewer entries than that (or none), print a 'could not parse the findings' verdict and return a non-zero exit (1, or a new code) rather than 0. Add a test with a body whose header counts findings but whose `` markup the regex does not match. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

9. A finding titled with 'Resolved' counts as fixed 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>_STRUCK matches the bare substring Resolved anywhere in a finding's title, and
>Finding.resolved uses it to leave a finding out of the open count. An open finding whose title
>contains that word (e.g. "Resolved paths escape the root") is printed as resolved, drops out of
>verdict: N of M findings open, and the diff reports it as resolved since k.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[src/hands/hosted.py[57]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/pull/4/files#diff-12a5dbbc969c160015a0fe085926cb598038c83131b13d5d84d1da86343eed7eR57-R57) > >```diff >+_STRUCK = re.compile(r"|||~~|Resolved") >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>docs/QODO-EXTRACTION.md says the bot marks a resolved finding by striking it through with `✓
>Resolved. The regex is much looser: any Resolved substring counts. _plain` itself strips only
>the exact ✓ Resolved string.
>
> > [src/hands/hosted.py\[51-85\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/d50af2a99203bf98a3b4a628daf4227b1466e8c4/src/hands/hosted.py/#L51-L85) > [docs/QODO-EXTRACTION.md\[12-12\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/d50af2a99203bf98a3b4a628daf4227b1466e8c4/docs/QODO-EXTRACTION.md/#L12-L12) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >`_STRUCK` treats any title containing `Resolved` as a resolved finding. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- src/hands/hosted.py[57-57] > >## Recommended Fix >Replace the bare `Resolved` alternative with the bot's actual marker, e.g. `✓ Resolved` (or `✓\s*Resolved`), and keep the strike-through tags. Add a test for an open finding whose title contains the word 'Resolved'. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

10. Each wait-loop retry writes another archive 🐞 Bug ⚙ Maintainability
>
>Description >
> >
>When the bot has posted its summary but not yet its Code Review comment, run archives a new <k>
>directory and only then returns EXIT_NOT_YET. The protocol and the brief tell the agent to rerun
>the command every minute for up to ten minutes on exit 3, so each retry adds another numbered
>snapshot, which gets committed, and the next diff compares against a partial fetch rather than the
>builder's real one.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[src/hands/hosted.py[R376-379]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/pull/4/files#diff-12a5dbbc969c160015a0fe085926cb598038c83131b13d5d84d1da86343eed7eR376-R379) > >```diff >+ if review is None: >+ print("verdict: no Code Review comment from the bot yet — no verdict; the " >+ "inline comments are not one (§39)", file=out) >+ return EXIT_NOT_YET >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The archive is written at line 328, before the review is None check at line 376. The CLI help
>(cli.py) promises exit 3 "with nothing written when the bot has not commented yet", and
>REVIEW-PROTOCOL.md calls "no Code Review comment yet" the same wait as exit 3, to be rerun once a
>minute.
>
> > [src/hands/hosted.py\[315-379\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/d50af2a99203bf98a3b4a628daf4227b1466e8c4/src/hands/hosted.py/#L315-L379) > [templates/REVIEW-PROTOCOL.md\[59-63\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/d50af2a99203bf98a3b4a628daf4227b1466e8c4/templates/REVIEW-PROTOCOL.md/#L59-L63) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. ### The AI Code Review Platform

## Get Started
Simply sign into Github and click the "Configure" button. Check out our documentation for more info: https://docs.qodo.ai/get-started.

## Overview
Qodo automatically reviews every GitHub pull request, identifies logic bugs, edge cases, security issues, and code quality problems, and provides actionable suggestions your team can apply immediately.

Install in minutes. Integrates seamlessly into your existing workflows.

## Qodo is designed for developers who:
- Handle frequent pull requests and need reliable review coverage
- Balance code quality with fast delivery
- Work in complex, multi-repo systems
- Use AI-generated code and need stronger guardrails
- Build production software where reliability matters

## Qodo Capabilities
- ## Automated PR Analysis
  - Reviews every pull request automatically
  - No manual trigger required

- ## Context-Aware Code Review
  - Understands cross-file changes
  - Detects architectural inconsistencies

- ## Actionable Suggestions
  - Concrete code fixes
  - Clear explanations
  - Prioritized feedback

- ## Security & Reliability Checks
  - Identifies risky patterns
  - Reduces attack surface area
